names.official: Republic of the Union of Myanmar

summary: Most visitors need Myanmar's official tourist eVisa — 28 days, US$50, open to roughly 100 nationalities and valid only for arrival at the main international airports or the Kawthaung land border — while most ASEAN passport holders enter visa-free for short stays (Malaysians need the eVisa). Canada says land crossings may close with little or no notice or be restricted to nationals of neighbouring states, and the UK advises against all travel to much of the country.

notes: The UK government says there are strict regulations on bringing in and using drones: do not try to enter Myanmar with one unless you have the permits before you travel. Australia's Smartraveller says drones have been seized by customs and tourists arrested for flying them.

You must declare gold, gems and jewellery to customs on arrival and get import and export permits (UK government). Canada says exporting gems is illegal and a permit is needed to buy or possess cultural or archaeological artefacts.

payments.text: The UK government says Myanmar is largely a cash-based society: many ATMs do not accept international cards, many shops take only cash, and you should phone ahead if you want to pay a hotel or restaurant by card. Canada says US dollars are widely accepted but only as new, unmarked, undamaged notes, and that changing money anywhere other than an authorised exchange is illegal.

safety.text: Myanmar is in armed conflict following the 2021 military coup. Canada strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar, and the UK advises against all travel to much of the country. Canada reports regime airstrikes and drone strikes causing civilian casualties; the UK says some areas are under martial law or curfews, and both warn of a risk of arbitrary detention.

tips.text: Canada strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar and Australia says do not travel; the UK advises against all travel to much of the country, including Rakhine, Kachin, Chin and Shan North, and against all but essential travel to Mandalay Region. Canada reports regime airstrikes and drone strikes, and says embassy staff need government permission to travel outside Yangon.

Canada advises against all travel to Myanmar, including through its land borders, and says crossings may close with little or no notice or be restricted to nationals of the neighbouring state. The eVisa is valid only for arrival at Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports and the Kawthaung land checkpoint.

Bring enough US dollars for your stay: the UK government says Myanmar is largely cash-based and many ATMs do not accept international cards, and that notes must be in good condition, without pen marks, folds or tears. Exchange counters may refuse notes whose serial numbers start AB or CB.

The UK government says the authorities control internet access and periodically cut it off entirely, and that some services, including Facebook and WhatsApp, are blocked. Canada advises charging your phone and carrying power banks in case of internet, communication and power outages.
The UK government says to remove shoes and socks before entering a pagoda or monastery, and that shorts, short skirts and sleeveless tops can cause offence at religious sites.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Myanmar?
faq.answer: Almost certainly yes. Around 100 nationalities — including the US, UK, EU countries, Australia and most of Asia — can apply for the 28-day tourist eVisa (US$50) at evisa.moip.gov.mm. Most ASEAN citizens enter visa-free for 14 days (Vietnam and Singapore 30). Everyone else needs an embassy visa.

faq.question: Can I enter Myanmar overland?
faq.answer: Mostly no. Canada advises against all travel to Myanmar, including through its land borders, and says crossings may close with little or no notice or be restricted to nationals of the neighbouring state. The eVisa is valid only at Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports and the Kawthaung land checkpoint.

faq.question: Is Myanmar safe to visit?
faq.answer: No. Canada strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar and Australia says do not travel; the UK advises against all travel to much of the country. Canada reports an escalating conflict with regime airstrikes, drone strikes and civilian casualties, and improvised explosive devices have been used in Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw. Check your government's advice before booking.

faq.question: How long does the Myanmar eVisa take?
faq.answer: Processing takes at least 3 working days (Myanmar time), counted from the acknowledgement email sent after you submit and pay. Apply only through the official portal, evisa.moip.gov.mm — third-party sites charge more and add nothing. Print the approval letter to show on arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend a Myanmar tourist visa?
faq.answer: The 28-day tourist eVisa is not formally extendable. The official eVisa notice publishes no overstay penalty, so do not count on settling an overstay at departure. Plan to leave within your permitted stay.
